exercises.name: Counting Down Sleep Breath
instructions: Lie down in bed or a comfortable reclined position and close your eyes.
Inhale slowly through your nose, then exhale while silently counting 'ten.'
Inhale again, then exhale while counting 'nine,' continuing to count down with each exhale.
If you lose track, simply restart from ten — the goal is a slow, wandering mind, not a perfect count.

exercises.name: Cooling Sitali Breath
instructions: Sit comfortably and curl the sides of your tongue inward to form a tube, then stick it slightly past your lips.
Inhale slowly through the curled tongue, feeling a cool sensation on your tongue.
Close your mouth and exhale slowly through your nose.
Repeat for the full duration to help cool the body and calm the mind.
exercises.caution: If you can't curl your tongue, sip air through slightly parted, pursed lips instead.

exercises.name: Three-Part Breath (Dirga Pranayama)
instructions: Lie down or sit tall and place one hand on your belly and one on your chest.
Inhale slowly, filling your belly first, then your ribcage, then your upper chest.
Exhale slowly in reverse order, releasing your chest first, then ribs, then belly.
Continue this three-part wave of breath, moving slowly and smoothly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Body Scan Breathing
instructions: Lie down comfortably and take a few natural breaths to settle in.
With each inhale, bring your attention to a new part of your body, starting at your feet.
With each exhale, consciously relax that body part before moving your attention upward on the next inhale.
Continue scanning up through your legs, torso, arms, and head until the timer ends.

exercises.name: Segmented Exhale Breathing (Viloma)
instructions: Sit or lie down comfortably and take one full inhale through your nose.
Exhale slowly, but pause briefly two or three times partway through the exhale instead of releasing it all at once.
Resume the exhale after each pause until your lungs feel empty, then inhale normally.
Repeat the segmented exhale for the full duration.

exercises.name: Progressive Relaxation Breath
instructions: Lie down comfortably and take a slow breath in while gently tensing your feet and calves.
Exhale fully while releasing that tension completely, feeling the muscles go heavy.
Inhale again, tensing the next muscle group up (thighs, then glutes, then abs, and so on), and exhale to release.
Work your way up your whole body, pairing each tense-and-release with one slow breath cycle.

exercises.name: Left-Nostril Calming Breath (Chandra Bhedana)
instructions: Sit comfortably and bring your right hand up, folding your index and middle fingers into your palm.
Close your right nostril gently with your right thumb and inhale slowly through your left nostril only.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger, release your thumb, and exhale slowly through your right nostril.
Continue inhaling only through the left and exhaling only through the right for the full duration — this pattern is traditionally used to calm and cool the body before rest.

exercises.name: Standing IT Band Side Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand tall next to a wall for balance and cross your left leg behind your right leg.
Reach your left arm overhead and lean your torso to the right, away from your left hip.
Push your left hip out to the side as you lean, feeling the stretch along the outside of your left thigh.
Hold, then return to center slowly and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing IT Band Side Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand tall next to a wall for balance and cross your right leg behind your left leg.
Reach your right arm overhead and lean your torso to the left, away from your right hip.
Push your right hip out to the side as you lean, feeling the stretch along the outside of your right thigh.
Hold, then return to center slowly and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Dynamic Standing Leg Swings
instructions: Stand next to a wall or sturdy support and hold on lightly with one hand.
Swing your outside leg forward and backward in a smooth, controlled pendulum motion, keeping your knee soft.
Let the swing grow gradually taller as your hips loosen, without forcing the range of motion.
After the set time, turn around and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.caution: Keep the motion controlled, not kicking — this is a warm-up mobilizer, not a max-range stretch.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Circles
instructions: Stand with your hands on your hips, feet a little wider than shoulder-width apart.
Shift your hips in a slow, wide circle, first tracing several circles clockwise.
Keep your upper body relatively still and let the movement come from your hips.
Reverse direction and circle counter-clockwise for the remaining time.

exercises.name: Runner's Lunge with Rotation (Left)
instructions: Step your left foot forward into a deep lunge, back leg straight and back heel lifted.
Place your right hand on the floor or a block inside your left foot for support.
Reach your left arm up toward the ceiling, rotating your chest open to the left.
Hold, feeling the stretch through your right hip flexor and your rotated torso, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Runner's Lunge with Rotation (Right)
instructions: Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, back leg straight and back heel lifted.
Place your left hand on the floor or a block inside your right foot for support.
Reach your right arm up toward the ceiling, rotating your chest open to the right.
Hold, feeling the stretch through your left hip flexor and your rotated torso, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about a foot away, with your left foot planted flat behind you.
Keeping your left heel on the ground, bend your left knee forward toward the wall.
Ease your knee forward until you feel a stretch through the front of your ankle and up your shin.
Hold, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about a foot away, with your right foot planted flat behind you.
Keeping your right heel on the ground, bend your right knee forward toward the wall.
Ease your knee forward until you feel a stretch through the front of your ankle and up your shin.
Hold, then release and switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: 20-20-20 Focus Shift
instructions: Sit comfortably and look at something roughly 20 feet (6 metres) away.
Let your eyes settle on it without straining to focus.
Hold your gaze there for about 20 seconds, breathing slowly.
Blink softly a few times to refresh your eyes.
Return to your near task; repeat whenever your eyes feel tired.
exercises.caution: This is a rest break, not a treatment. See an eye professional for persistent eye pain or changes in vision.

exercises.name: Gentle Eye Rolls
instructions: Sit tall and keep your head still, looking straight ahead.
Slowly move your gaze up, then trace a smooth circle: up, right, down, left.
Keep the movement slow and comfortable — never forced.
Complete 3 to 4 slow circles, then reverse direction.
Blink and let your eyes rest for a moment when finished.
exercises.caution: Stop if you feel dizzy or any eye strain. Skip if you have a recent eye injury or eye condition.

exercises.name: Jaw-Open Temporalis Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall with relaxed shoulders.
Slowly open your mouth as wide as is comfortable and pain-free.
Feel a gentle stretch through the temples and jaw.
Hold for about 5 seconds, then slowly close.
Repeat gently and slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop if your jaw clicks, locks, or hurts, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Resisted Jaw Opening
instructions: Place your thumb or two fingers gently under your chin.
Slowly open your mouth against light resistance from your fingers.
Use only a small, gentle amount of pressure — this is not a strength test.
Open a short way, hold for 3 seconds, then slowly close.
Repeat calmly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Use very light resistance and stay pain-free. Stop if you feel clicking, locking, or pain, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Side-to-Side Jaw Glide
instructions: Relax your jaw with your teeth slightly apart.
Slowly glide your lower jaw to one side as far as is comfortable.
Return to centre, then glide gently to the other side.
Keep the movement small, smooth, and pain-free.
Continue slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently within a comfortable range. Stop if the jaw clicks, locks, or hurts, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Tongue-Up Controlled Open/Close
instructions: Rest the tip of your tongue lightly on the roof of your mouth, behind your front teeth.
Keeping the tongue there, slowly open your mouth only as far as it stays in contact.
This keeps the jaw opening controlled and centred.
Hold briefly, then slowly close.
Repeat calmly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep it slow and pain-free. Stop if you feel clicking, locking, or pain, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Frontalis Release
instructions: Rest the pads of your fingers gently across your forehead.
Let your eyebrows relax downward as you breathe out slowly.
Apply light, still pressure — no rubbing or pulling on the skin.
Hold and breathe slowly, letting the forehead soften.
Release gently after the hold and repeat.
exercises.caution: Use light pressure only. Avoid if you have a skin condition or injury on the forehead.

exercises.name: Physiological Sigh (Double Inhale Exhale)
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably with your shoulders relaxed.
Inhale deeply through your nose until your lungs feel full.
Without exhaling, take a second short, sharp inhale to top off your lungs completely.
Exhale slowly and fully through your mouth, letting your shoulders and jaw release.
Pause briefly, then begin the next double inhale.
Repeat the double-inhale, long-exhale pattern for the full duration.

exercises.name: Resonant Frequency Breathing (6 Breaths per Minute)
instructions: Sit upright in a relaxed, supported position.
Inhale gently through your nose for a slow count of 5.
Exhale gently through your nose or mouth for a slow count of 5.
Keep the breath smooth and unforced — an even, unhurried rhythm matters more than precise counting.
Let your belly and chest rise and fall together naturally.
Continue the steady in-and-out rhythm for the full duration.
exercises.caution: If counting to 5 feels strained, shorten the count until the breath feels comfortable.

exercises.name: Right-Nostril Energizing Breath (Surya Bhedana)
instructions: Sit tall in a comfortable cross-legged or chair position.
Rest your left hand on your knee and bring your right hand toward your nose.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger and inhale slowly through your right nostril.
Close your right nostril with your thumb, release your left nostril, and exhale slowly through the left side.
Continue inhaling through the right nostril and exhaling through the left for the full duration.
Let your breath stay smooth and unforced throughout.
exercises.caution: Skip this practice if you have high blood pressure, feel anxious or overheated, or are practicing close to bedtime — it's energizing, not calming.

exercises.name: Skull Shining Breath (Kapalabhati)
instructions: Sit tall with a long spine and relaxed shoulders.
Take one slow, deep inhale to begin.
Sharply contract your lower belly to push a short, forceful exhale out through your nose.
Let the inhale that follows happen passively and naturally as your belly relaxes.
Continue the quick, rhythmic pumping exhales for about 20 pumps, then return to normal breathing and rest.
Repeat for one or two more rounds if comfortable, resting between each.
exercises.caution: Avoid if pregnant, or if you have high blood pressure, a hernia, or recent abdominal or eye surgery. Stop immediately if you feel lightheaded.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch (Left Lead Leg)
instructions: From standing, step your left foot forward into a deep lunge, extending your right leg straight behind you.
Place both hands on the floor inside your left foot to support your balance.
Drop your right hip toward the floor to deepen the stretch through the back leg's hip flexor.
Rotate your torso and reach your left arm toward the ceiling, opening your chest to the left.
Return your hand to the floor, then straighten your left leg to feel the stretch shift into the hamstring.
Bend the left knee again and repeat the reach-and-straighten cycle smoothly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move within a pain-free range and skip the torso rotation if you feel any low-back strain.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch (Right Lead Leg)
instructions: From standing, step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, extending your left leg straight behind you.
Place both hands on the floor inside your right foot to support your balance.
Drop your left hip toward the floor to deepen the stretch through the back leg's hip flexor.
Rotate your torso and reach your right arm toward the ceiling, opening your chest to the right.
Return your hand to the floor, then straighten your right leg to feel the stretch shift into the hamstring.
Bend the right knee again and repeat the reach-and-straighten cycle smoothly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move within a pain-free range and skip the torso rotation if you feel any low-back strain.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Rotation with Overhead Reach (Left)
instructions: Sit tall on a chair or the floor with your feet grounded and spine long.
Reach your left arm straight overhead, lengthening the left side of your body.
Rest your right hand on your left knee or the chair for support.
Gently rotate your torso to the left, leading with your chest, while keeping the overhead reach.
Hold the rotation and reach, breathing slowly into the stretch along your side and back.
Release back to center with control.
exercises.caution: Rotate only as far as feels comfortable, and avoid forcing the twist if you have a back condition.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Rotation with Overhead Reach (Right)
instructions: Sit tall on a chair or the floor with your feet grounded and spine long.
Reach your right arm straight overhead, lengthening the right side of your body.
Rest your left hand on your right knee or the chair for support.
Gently rotate your torso to the right, leading with your chest, while keeping the overhead reach.
Hold the rotation and reach, breathing slowly into the stretch along your side and back.
Release back to center with control.
exercises.caution: Rotate only as far as feels comfortable, and avoid forcing the twist if you have a back condition.

exercises.name: Standing Adductor Rock (Side-to-Side)
instructions: Stand with your feet spread wide apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Shift your weight onto your left leg, bending the left knee while keeping your right leg straight, feeling the stretch along the inner right thigh.
Rock your weight across to the right leg, bending the right knee while straightening the left leg.
Keep your chest lifted and hands resting on your thighs or hips for balance throughout.
Continue rocking smoothly side to side for the full duration.

exercises.name: Standing Tibialis Raise (Toe Lifts)
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, near a wall or chair for balance if needed.
Keeping your heels planted, lift the balls of your feet and toes up off the floor as high as you can.
Hold briefly at the top, feeling the engagement along the front of your shins.
Lower your toes back down with control.
Repeat the lift-and-lower rhythm for the full duration.

exercises.name: Thumb Extension Stretch (Left)
instructions: Hold your left hand up with fingers relaxed.
Use your right hand to gently bend your left thumb back and down, away from your palm.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the base of the thumb.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Thumb Extension Stretch (Right)
instructions: Hold your right hand up with fingers relaxed.
Use your left hand to gently bend your right thumb back and down, away from your palm.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the base of the thumb.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Hook Fist Tendon Glide
instructions: Hold both hands up in front of you with fingers straight.
Bend only your first and second knuckles to form a hook shape, keeping your knuckles at the base of the fingers straight.
Hold for 3-5 seconds, then straighten your fingers fully.
Repeat the hook-and-straighten motion for the full duration to glide the finger tendons.

exercises.name: Fist-to-Fan Tendon Gliding Flow
instructions: Start with both hands in loose, relaxed fists.
Slowly open your fingers and spread them as wide as you can, like a fan.
Hold the spread for 2-3 seconds, then curl back into a fist.
Repeat the fist-to-fan sequence slowly for the full duration.

exercises.name: Towel Scrunch (Toe Flexor Stretch)
instructions: Sit in a chair with a small towel laid flat on the floor under your feet.
Using only your toes, scrunch the towel toward you, gripping and pulling it inward.
Release and reset the towel flat, then repeat.
Continue scrunching for the full duration to work the small muscles under your feet.

exercises.name: Big Toe Extension Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit and cross your left ankle over your right knee.
Use your hand to gently pull your left big toe upward and back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the sole and big toe.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Big Toe Extension Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit and cross your right ankle over your left knee.
Use your hand to gently pull your right big toe upward and back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the sole and big toe.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Seated Toe-to-Shin Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit toward the edge of a chair and extend your left leg with your heel on the floor.
Reach down and gently pull the ball of your left foot and toes back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the bottom of the foot and calf.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Seated Toe-to-Shin Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit toward the edge of a chair and extend your right leg with your heel on the floor.
Reach down and gently pull the ball of your right foot and toes back toward your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the bottom of the foot and calf.
Release and repeat 2-3 times.

exercises.name: Jaw Relaxation Drop
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably and let your shoulders relax.
Rest your tongue lightly on the roof of your mouth just behind your front teeth.
Let your lips stay gently closed while allowing your back teeth to come apart, letting your jaw hang loose.
Breathe slowly and hold this passive, relaxed position for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently within a comfortable, pain-free range. Stop if your jaw clicks, locks, or hurts, and see a dentist for diagnosed TMJ problems.

exercises.name: Circular Temple Self-Massage
instructions: Place your fingertips lightly on your temples, just beside your eyebrows.
Make small, slow circular motions with light pressure.
Circle in one direction for half the time, then reverse direction.
Breathe slowly throughout to help release tension.
exercises.caution: Use gentle pressure only. Skip if you have a headache disorder that worsens with touch or any scalp or skin condition.

exercises.name: Figure-8 Eye Tracking
instructions: Sit comfortably and hold your head still, facing forward.
Without moving your head, trace a slow, wide figure-8 shape in the air with your eyes.
Complete a few slow figure-8s in one direction, then reverse.
Keep the motion smooth and unhurried for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Stop if you feel dizzy or any eye strain. Skip if you have a recent eye injury or eye condition.

exercises.name: Full Scalp Massage (Tension Release)
instructions: Place your fingertips on your scalp, spread wide like a claw.
Press lightly and move your scalp in small circles over the skull, not just sliding over the hair.
Work slowly from your hairline back toward the crown and down toward the base of your skull.
Breathe slowly and keep the pressure light and comfortable throughout.
exercises.caution: Use gentle pressure only. Skip if you have a headache disorder that worsens with touch or any scalp or skin condition.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch (Rotation Flow)
instructions: Sit on the floor with both knees bent, one leg in front of you and one out to the side, each at roughly 90 degrees.
Keeping your chest tall, lift both knees slightly and rotate them to switch sides, so the front leg becomes the side leg and vice versa.
Lower down into the new position with control.
Continue switching sides smoothly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move with control rather than momentum, and keep the motion pain-free through the hips and knees.

exercises.name: Shoulder Pendulum Swing (Left)
instructions: Lean forward slightly and support yourself with your right hand on a chair or table.
Let your left arm hang loose and relaxed toward the floor.
Gently swing the arm in small circles, letting gravity do the work rather than using muscle effort.
Continue the slow, passive swinging for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Shoulder Pendulum Swing (Right)
instructions: Lean forward slightly and support yourself with your left hand on a chair or table.
Let your right arm hang loose and relaxed toward the floor.
Gently swing the arm in small circles, letting gravity do the work rather than using muscle effort.
Continue the slow, passive swinging for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Lumbar Side Glide (Lateral Shift)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Keeping your shoulders level and facing forward, shift your hips directly to one side without bending or twisting.
Hold briefly, feeling the stretch along one side of your lower back, then glide back to center.
Repeat, shifting to the other side, alternating for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move within a comfortable range and stop if you feel sharp or radiating pain.

exercises.name: Neck Isometric Front-and-Back Press
instructions: Sit or stand tall and place one palm flat against your forehead.
Gently press your head forward into your hand without letting your head actually move, holding for 5 seconds.
Release, then place a hand behind your head and gently press backward into it without moving your head, holding for 5 seconds.
Alternate front and back presses for the full duration, keeping the effort light.
exercises.caution: Use only gentle, pain-free pressure and stop if you feel dizziness or sharp pain.

exercises.name: Seated Neck Half-Circles (Ear-to-Shoulder Arc)
instructions: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly drop your chin toward your chest, then arc your head so your right ear moves toward your right shoulder.
Continue the slow arc back through center to bring your left ear toward your left shoulder.
Keep the motion in the front half only — avoid tilting your head backward — and repeat slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Move gently and stop if you feel dizziness or sharp pain. Keep the arc in front, not tilting backward.

exercises.name: Table-Edge Bicep Stretch (Left)
instructions: Stand beside a sturdy table with your left arm straight and your palm flat on the table edge behind you, fingers pointing backward.
Keeping your arm straight, slowly turn your body away from the table.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of your upper arm.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Table-Edge Bicep Stretch (Right)
instructions: Stand beside a sturdy table with your right arm straight and your palm flat on the table edge behind you, fingers pointing backward.
Keeping your arm straight, slowly turn your body away from the table.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of your upper arm.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Cross-Body Triceps Press (Left)
instructions: Reach your left arm across your chest, keeping it straight and at shoulder height.
Use your right forearm to press your left arm closer to your chest.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the back of the left upper arm and shoulder.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Standing Cross-Body Triceps Press (Right)
instructions: Reach your right arm across your chest, keeping it straight and at shoulder height.
Use your left forearm to press your right arm closer to your chest.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch through the back of the right upper arm and shoulder.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Seated Assisted Tibialis Stretch (Left)
instructions: Sit with your left ankle crossed over your right knee.
Use your hand to gently point your left foot and toes downward and away from your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of the shin.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Seated Assisted Tibialis Stretch (Right)
instructions: Sit with your right ankle crossed over your left knee.
Use your hand to gently point your right foot and toes downward and away from your shin.
Hold for 15-20 seconds, feeling the stretch along the front of the shin.
Release and repeat 2-3 times, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Active Shoulder Shrug & Release (Left)
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Slowly raise your left shoulder up toward your left ear as far as comfortable.
Hold for 3-5 seconds, feeling the contraction, then let it drop and fully relax down.
Repeat the shrug-and-release for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Active Shoulder Shrug & Release (Right)
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides.
Slowly raise your right shoulder up toward your right ear as far as comfortable.
Hold for 3-5 seconds, feeling the contraction, then let it drop and fully relax down.
Repeat the shrug-and-release for the full duration, then switch sides on another round.

exercises.name: Grip and Release (Hand Squeeze Stretch)
instructions: Hold both hands out in front of you, relaxed.
Squeeze both hands into firm fists and hold for 3-5 seconds.
Release and spread your fingers wide open, holding for 3-5 seconds.
Repeat the squeeze-and-release cycle for the full duration.

exercises.name: Standing Waist Twist (Dynamic Rotation Flow)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and knees soft, arms relaxed and swinging loosely.
Gently rotate your torso to one side, letting your arms swing naturally with the motion.
Rotate back through center and continue to the other side.
Keep the motion light and controlled, alternating sides for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep the twist gentle and controlled — this is a mobility warm-up, not a forceful stretch.

exercises.name: Wall Slide (Shoulder Blade Mobility)
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your arms raised to form a 'W' shape, elbows and wrists touching the wall.
Slowly slide your arms up the wall into a 'Y' shape, keeping your elbows and wrists in contact with the wall as long as possible.
Slide back down to the starting 'W' position with control.
Repeat the slide up and down slowly for the full duration.
exercises.caution: Keep the motion pain-free and only slide as high as you can while keeping your arms touching the wall.

exercises.name: Triangle Breathing (3-3-3)
instructions: Sit comfortably with your back straight.
Inhale slowly through your nose for 3 counts.
Hold gently for 3 counts.
Exhale slowly through your nose or mouth for 3 counts.
Repeat the three-count cycle for the full duration.

exercises.name: So-Hum Mantra Breath
instructions: Sit comfortably with your eyes closed and your spine tall.
As you inhale slowly through your nose, silently say 'So' to yourself.
As you exhale slowly, silently say 'Hum' to yourself.
Let your breath set the pace rather than forcing it, continuing the silent 'So-Hum' for the full duration.

exercises.name: Breath Counting Meditation
instructions: Sit comfortably with your eyes closed or softly focused downward.
Breathe naturally, and silently count '1' at the end of your first exhale.
Continue counting up by one at the end of each exhale, up to 10.
When you reach 10, or if you lose track, simply start again at 1.

exercises.name: Segmented Inhale Breathing (Viloma 2)
instructions: Sit or lie down comfortably and exhale fully to start.
Inhale slowly, but pause briefly two or three times partway through the inhale instead of breathing in all at once.
Once your lungs feel full, exhale slowly and smoothly in one continuous breath.
Repeat the segmented inhale for the full duration.

exercises.name: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding Breath
instructions: Sit comfortably and take one slow breath in and out to settle.
Breathing slowly, silently notice 5 things you can see around you.
Continue breathing slowly as you notice 4 things you can hear, then 3 things you can feel touching your body.
Finish by noticing 2 things you can smell and 1 thing you can taste, keeping your breath slow and even throughout.
exercises.caution: This is a grounding technique for calm attention, not a treatment for anxiety or panic disorders — seek professional support if you need it.
